assets.role: Neutral registration master (approved)
notes: Human approved 2026-07-10 as the v01.01.F0 neutral registration master, after Fable visual review: 96/128/256 px reads verified over stage color, residual fringe re-verified at exactly 7 px (dry-run), warm-brown outline and top-left lighting invariants pass, feet baseline measurable at y=1007.

Review findings for F0.2: define the head unit operationally before freezing anchors (measured head-with-hair ratio 0.507 vs contract 0.45); canonical hand-on-hip pose means upper-garment masks must respect the bent character-right arm, and the free character-LEFT hand (screen right, tattoo forearm) is the primary held-item socket - corrected 2026-07-10 during the F0.2.1 anchor review, the original note had the handedness mirrored.
Anchors measured and frozen 2026-07-10 (F0.2.1): docs/art/contracts/mara-v5-registration-measurements.json. Do not move them after this point without a new registration master.

assets.role: Allowed-edit mask for garment edit-on-template generation
notes: Generated by tools/art/make-garment-mask.mjs, not hand-painted: regenerate from the master rather than editing the PNG directly if the master ever changes.

Segments the neutral tank+shorts by low-saturation/mid-luminance color, guarded above the chin and below the shorts hem, seeded from interior-only pixels to avoid the antialiased silhouette edge, then dilated 16px to give a replacement garment room past the skin-tight neutral outfit.

Editable region is 3.46% of canvas, contained to the torso/hip band with no bleed into face, hair, hands, or feet - verified by 6 node tests (make-garment-mask.node-tests.mjs) and visually via mara_v5_garment_mask_preview.png.

Internal convention only (white opaque = editable): this is what extract-edit-layer.mjs validates against. For uploading to an actual image-editing API, use mara-v5-garment-mask-openai instead - the two use inverted alpha conventions and are not interchangeable.
Does not itself need human approval - it is a technical editing boundary, not a creative asset; the garment that will be generated inside it does need approval (character-garment-proof gate).

assets.role: OpenAI images.edit-convention copy of the garment mask
notes: Same editable region as mara-v5-garment-mask, alpha polarity inverted: alpha 0 (transparent) = edit, alpha 255 (opaque) = preserve - OpenAI's images.edit contract, confirmed by the user 2026-07-11 (RGB is not read by the API, only alpha; a mid-value alpha means partial edit, so this file is kept strictly binary).

Preserved pixels carry the master's own RGB so the file previews as the character photo with a see-through hole over the tank+shorts, not a flat color swatch - the usual visual convention for an inpainting mask.

Do not confuse with mara-v5-garment-mask: uploading the internal-convention file to the API would make it regenerate the face/hair/pose and preserve only the garment - the exact opposite of the intent.
Generated by the same tools/art/make-garment-mask.mjs run (buildOpenAiMask); 2 dedicated node tests assert the alpha inversion and the RGB source.

assets.role: Allowed-edit mask for hair restyle edit-on-template generation
notes: Generated by tools/art/make-hair-mask.mjs. Geometric, not color-segmented like the garment mask - a new hairstyle's silhouette doesn't resemble the current curly hair, so segmenting by matching the existing hair color would be too restrictive.

A generous oval around and above the head (center 628,380, semi-axes 340x310px, well beyond the current hair's measured bounds) minus a protected face oval (eyes, eyebrows, nose, mouth, ears, cheeks - center 628,465 matching the headPivot anchor, semi-axes 185x165px, landmarks measured off a 2x zoomed gridded render, not guessed), clipped at y<=560 so it can never overlap the approved garment mask's editable region.
12.70% of canvas editable. 4 node tests verify protected landmarks stay untouched, the shoulder clip holds, and the region size is sane.

Known limitation for the prompt: a hairstyle whose silhouette droops past the shoulder clip line (long hair, braids reaching the collar) will leave a remnant of the OLD curly hair visible below the clip, the same failure mode as garment_v1's dress overflowing its mask - pick a hairstyle that stays within head+ear height for a clean first proof.

assets.role: OpenAI images.edit-convention copy of the hair mask
notes: Same editable region as mara-v5-hair-mask, alpha polarity inverted (alpha 0 = edit, alpha 255 = preserve) for the OpenAI images.edit contract. Upload this one, not the internal-convention file.
Verified by direct pixel sampling: top-of-hair alpha=0 (editable), eye-region alpha=255 (preserved).

assets.role: Allowed-edit mask for expression edit-on-template generation
notes: Generated by tools/art/make-expression-mask.mjs. Geometric union of 3 ellipses (left eye+eyebrow, right eye+eyebrow, mouth), landmarks measured off the same 2x zoomed gridded render used for the hair mask.

Deliberately small (2.41% of canvas) and does NOT cover skin/cheeks/face-outline - per the contract's zOrder, face_expression is a distinct layer from skin_detail; only the features that actually change between expressions are editable. Nose, ears, hair, and skin tone stay locked.
4 node tests verify both eyes and the mouth are covered, the nose/ears/hair stay protected, and the region doesn't creep down into the neck/garment area.

assets.role: Approved character-garment-proof: first edit-on-template garment layer
notes: Extracted layer (garment pixels only, inside the mask) from docs/art/pilot/raw/garment_v2.1.png, generated externally via an image-editing API using mara_v5_garment_mask_openai.png. Two prior attempts (garment_v1.png, garment_v2.png) were rejected: v1 drew a dress that overflowed the mask's hem (clipped in a straight line) plus heavy global drift; v2 fit the mask correctly but had a broad, uniform skin-tone shift across arms/legs.

Passed extract-edit-layer.mjs after the validator itself was recalibrated with real measurements from these three attempts: silhouette mismatch 0.133% (cap 0.5%), color drift 0.842% (cap 5%), severe color drift 0.256% (cap 0.3%) - see extract-layer-lib.mjs's header for the full reasoning on why silhouette and color drift are checked independently.

Composite (master + this layer) reviewed at 96/128/256px: garment (white crop top, black shorts) reads clearly at all three sizes, no seam artifacts at the mask boundary, face/hair/tattoo/arms/legs unaffected (sourced entirely from the master, never from the drifted edited image).

This is a layer, not a standalone asset: always composite over mara-v5-cutout-candidate, never use garment_v2.1.png (the full edited image) directly - that image has the color drift baked in everywhere outside the mask.

Human approved 2026-07-11: closes the character-garment-proof deliverable. Not yet wired into any runtime compositor - F0 has no modular paper-doll rendering system yet (island-scene.ts still renders the flat master sprite directly); that is separate future work, not implied by this approval.

The full F0.2.2 pilot-sequence gate (composed-pilot approval) still needs a hairstyle pair and two expressions proven the same way before it closes - this approval covers the garment deliverable only.
